narrative.overview:
The site is a newspaper's corrections column for the documents you agreed to. Every change is printed as a correction: what was removed is struck through in red pencil, what was added is underlined in blue pencil. The page is cool newsprint with true-ink rules, a masthead with a double rule, condensed newspaper-gothic headlines for everything we say, and a book serif for every word the companies wrote. It refuses both category defaults: the dark glowing dashboard and the cream "editorial" page.

Nothing is enclosed in cards. Sections open with a heavy ink rule and divide inside with hairlines, columns and whitespace. The one box on the page is the correction notice that prints the newest significant change, and one red pencil stroke travels slowly around its border. That stroke is the only thing that moves by itself. Recency is shown with fresh ink: a dot beside each date is solid when the change is new and fades to an outline over a year.

Density is a reading density: generous type, an 8px module under every gap and rule, and one plain sentence of purpose at the top.
keyCharacteristics: Cool newsprint ground, true ink rules, no cards.
Two editor's pencils: red strikes removed wording and marks Major; blue underlines added wording, links and fresh marks.
Archivo condensed (width axis) for our words; Source Serif 4 only for the companies' words.
One box (the correction), one moving thing (the red pencil stroke around it).
Fresh ink dots encode recency; the date is always written too.
Word-level redlines with real <del>/<ins> and hidden labels.

rules.name: The Two Pencils Rule
rules.body: Red means removed or Major; blue means added, clickable or fresh. Everything else is ink and grey. Filled buttons and "current" markers are ink, not blue.

rules.name: The Lightest Ink Rule
rules.body: faint (4.9:1 on newsprint) is the lightest text colour allowed. All text is at least 4.5:1 against its ground.

rules.name: The Whose Words Rule
rules.body: Our words are Archivo; the companies' words are Source Serif 4. Never the other way round, and no third family.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Sentence case everywhere. No all-caps labels and no small label above a heading: the heading says it.

rules.name: The Condensed Means Headline Rule
rules.body: Width tracks rank: 66% for page headlines, 70–72% for correction and section headings, 80–90% for names, tags and nav, 100% for reading text.

rules.name: The 8px Module Rule
rules.body: Gaps, padding and rule positions are multiples or clean halves of 8px (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 40).

rules.name: The Rules Not Cards Rule
rules.body: Sections open with a 3px ink rule and group inside with hairlines and whitespace. No cards, no tinted section backgrounds.

rules.name: The One Box Rule
rules.body: The correction is the only enclosed block on the page. Floating things (menus, search, tooltip, pinned bar) are boxed because they are not on the page.

rules.name: The Fresh Ink Rule
rules.body: A dot by each date shows how recent a change is: solid blue (scaled 1.15) within a month, a 55% tint within three months, a blue outline within a year, a grey hairline ring after that. Major changes use red at every step and keep a red outline when old. The date is always written beside it, and the feed footer explains the marks.

dos: Do open every section with a 3px ink rule and divide inside with 1px hairlines.
Do keep the correction the only box on the page, with its single red pencil stroke.
Do set the companies' words in Source Serif 4 and ours in condensed Archivo.

Do mark removed wording with <del> struck red and added wording with <ins> underlined blue, each with a hidden label and a proofreader's mark in the margin (blue caret, red dele loop, or slash and caret for an edited sentence).
Do show recency with fresh-ink dots and always write the date beside them.
Do keep tap targets at least 44px on phones, text at least 4.5:1, and stop all motion under reduced motion.
donts: Don't wrap content in cards, tinted panels or shadowed boxes; only floating menus, search, tooltips and the pinned bar are boxed.
Don't add motion that isn't a pencil marking something: no fades, slides or lifts for their own sake, and only one loop (the pencil around the correction).
Don't use red for anything but removed wording and Major, or blue for anything but added wording, links, fresh marks and pins.
Don't use dark glowing surfaces, glass, gradients or a cream "editorial" ground; the paper is cool newsprint.
Don't put a small label above a heading or use all-caps labels.
Don't use stat tiles or big numbers; say the size of a change in a sentence.
